title: Allow temporary changes to be made from a script only for the current session
line: Plasma scripts can now change a widget's or wallpaper's settings just for the current session with writeTemporaryConfig(), without saving them to disk.
explanation: Desktop scripts could only change widget, desktop and panel settings through writeConfig(), which saves every value to plasma-org.kde.plasma.desktop-appletsrc right away, so nothing could be changed for the current session only. Writing non-persistent KConfig entries alone isn't enough, because plasmashell reloads that file from disk whenever any widget's configuration changes. The new writeTemporaryConfig(key, value) on widgets, desktops and panels updates the widget's (or wallpaper's) live configuration and marks the value as already loaded, so it shows immediately, is never written to disk by later saves, and is gone after plasmashell restarts.

commits.message:
shell/scripting: add writeTemporaryConfig for session-only changes

Every config change made from a script was saved to disk, so a widget or
wallpaper couldn't be changed just for the current session. The new
writeTemporaryConfig() applies the value right away without saving it.

BUG: 518887

media.caption: Master: writeTemporaryConfig doesn't exist; writeConfig is the only way and it writes showSeconds=2 to appletsrc for good
Fix: temporary clock settings and wallpaper apply at once, appletsrc is untouched, and a plasmashell restart brings the original back
Master: the clock change from a script is saved immediately
Fix: temporary clock change stays applied (and unsaved) when another widget saves its own settings
